meanings.note: j'en ai assez = I've had enough, I'm fed up
Assez bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'enough'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Très bien = very well, fine. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
C'est bien. Invariable French adverb meaning 'well'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: bien sûr que + sentence = of course...

examples.text: Bien sûr que tu es fatiguée.
Bien sûr. Interflora, s'il vous plaît.

meanings.note: À bientôt = see you soon. Invariable French adverb meaning 'soon'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
Carte de visite. Feminine noun ('la carte', plural 'les cartes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'card'.
Carte bancaire. Feminine noun ('la carte', plural 'les cartes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'card'.
Feminine noun ('la carte', plural 'les cartes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'card'.

examples.trans: My card. Call me at the office.

examples.text: Vous avez la carte, s'il vous plaît?
examples.trans: Do you have the menu, please?

examples.text: Attends, regarde mes cartes de visite.
examples.trans: Wait, look at my business cards.

meanings.note: celle = feminine: celle de la semaine dernière

examples.text: Clémentine? Celle de la semaine dernière?
examples.trans: Clémentine? The one from last week?

meanings.note: Prendre contact = to make contact. Prefix 'con-'/'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Standard masculine noun meaning 'contact, touch'.

examples.text: Je n'aime pas trop le contact.
Je pourrais vous mettre en contact avec lui...
examples.trans: I could put you in touch with him...

meanings.note: D' before a vowel. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
le film de Tarantino = Tarantino's film
Also 'some': du sucre. Core French preposition meaning 'of', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Donner quelque chose à quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to give'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'donné').

examples.text: Fais du vélo! Ça donne des forces.
examples.trans: Ride a bike! It gives you energy.

meanings.note: Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation.

examples.text: Elle est débordée, ne l'embêtons pas.
examples.trans: She is swamped, let's not bother her.

meanings.note: tu es déjà venu? = have you been here before?
tu es déjà venu? = have you been here before?

examples.text: Elle avait déjà pris sa décision.
examples.trans: She had already made her decision.

examples.text: C'est tellement malhonnête! Elle avait déjà pris sa décision.
examples.trans: That's so dishonest! She'd already made her decision.

meanings.note: for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle
for a feminine noun: l'industrie... elle

examples.text: Écoute, c'est une industrie, et elle est pleine de requins.
examples.trans: Listen, it's an industry, and it's full of sharks.

meanings.note: Informal/familiar. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to bother'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'embêté').

examples.trans: You are doing this to annoy me.

examples.text: Tu fais ça juste pour m'embêter!
examples.trans: You're doing this just to annoy me!

meanings.note: en retard = late, en vacances = on holiday

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to send'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'envoyé').

examples.text: Oui, c'est envoyé. Voici la facture.
examples.trans: Yes, it's been sent. Here's the bill.

meanings.note: The t is never pronounced. French conjunction meaning 'and', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: for (duration): ça fait des mois que j'attends = I've been waiting for months
Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

meanings.en: faire la surprise à = to surprise
meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

meanings.en: ça fait trois semaines que = it's been three weeks since
meanings.note: With time. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to do, to make'.

examples.text: Ça fait une heure que j'attends.
examples.trans: I've been waiting for an hour.

meanings.note: en fait = in fact; tout à fait = completely, quite

examples.text: Oui, oui... C'est tout à fait moi, oui.
examples.trans: Yes, yes... That is completely me, yes.

related.gloss: in fact; tout à fait = completely, quite

meanings.en: to be needed, to be necessary
meanings.note: only with impersonal il: il faut + noun or infinitive

examples.text: Oui, mais il faut des autorisations. Ah, la paperasse française!
examples.trans: Yes, but you need permits. Ah, French paperwork!

meanings.note: for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Also in fixed phrases: il y a. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'he'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Never changes for plural. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'there is', common in natural conversation.
il y a trois semaines = three weeks ago

examples.text: Il y a une autre Clémentine?
Non, c'est la place de Samuel. Il est mort il y a six jours.
examples.trans: No, it's Samuel's place. He died six days ago.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: Mais oui! = of course!. French conjunction meaning 'but', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
Before the verb; m' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'me'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
merci beaucoup = thank you very much

examples.text: Merci beaucoup pour votre aide précieuse aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your valuable help today.

examples.text: Je te dis mille fois merci pour ce beau rôle!
examples.trans: I thank you a thousand times for this great role!

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: Idiomatic French interj expression meaning 'okay', frequent in natural conversational dialogue.

examples.text: OK, je vous envoie sa carte.
examples.trans: OK, I will send you her card.

examples.text: OK, comme ça tu évites de nous demander.

meanings.note: everyday speech, with a he/she verb form
General. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'we'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.en: to organize, to arrange, to set up
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to organize'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'organisé').

examples.trans: I want to set up a meeting.

examples.text: Si je lui dis ça, elle va organiser des manifestations!
examples.trans: If I tell her that, she's going to organise protests!

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'yes'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: second half of ne... pas; in speech ne is often dropped

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: Penser que... = to think that. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to think'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'pensé').
Penser à. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to think'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'pensé').

examples.text: Ils ont pensé que c'était mieux.
Ils ont pensé que ce serait mieux avec un homme.
examples.trans: They thought it would be better with a man.

meanings.note: permettre à quelqu'un de faire = to allow someone to do

examples.text: Mon amour-propre ne me le permet pas.
examples.trans: My pride will not allow it.

examples.text: Tout est permis, sauf la norme de la monogamie.
examples.trans: Everything is allowed, except the norm of monogamy.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'maybe'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.trans: Maybe it's all in my head.

meanings.note: before an infinitive: pour faire plaisir
+ infinitive: pour voir. Core French preposition meaning 'for', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.
C'est comme un rêve pour moi.
examples.trans: It's like a dream for me.

meanings.note: + infinitive. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'can, to be able to'.
conditional: tu pourrais, vous pourriez
informal, often at the end: pour faire quoi?, c'est quoi?

examples.text: Quoi, tu n'as pas encore lu le nouveau scénario?
examples.trans: What, you haven't read the new script yet?

examples.text: De quoi est-ce que vous parlez tous les deux?
examples.trans: What are the two of you talking about?

meanings.note: Faire une rencontre. Prefix 're-'/'ré-' marks repetition, return, or intensity. Standard feminine noun meaning 'meeting, encounter'.

examples.trans: I want to set up a meeting.

examples.text: Je veux organiser une rencontre avec Steven Spielberg, qui est à Paris.
examples.trans: I want to set up a meeting with Steven Spielberg, who is in Paris.

meanings.note: For the first time, or by chance. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to meet'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'rencontré').

examples.text: Je ne vais pas rencontrer quelqu'un ici.
examples.trans: I'm not going to meet anyone here.

examples.text: Et je ne vais pas rencontrer quelqu'un ici.
examples.trans: And I'm not going to meet anyone here.

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned, not the owner

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: Bien sûr = of course. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sure'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'sure'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'very'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: One person, formal. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'you'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Several people. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'you'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
je vous rappelle = I'll call you back
Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a ... mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Tu crois vraiment qu'il va accepter ce rôle?
examples.trans: Do you really think he is going to accept this role?

examples.text: Je suis vraiment désolée pour ce petit retard.
examples.trans: I am truly sorry for this slight delay.

meanings.note: Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Feminine noun ('la équipe', plural 'les équipes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'team'.

examples.trans: Yes, I have a great team.

meanings.note: The most common verb. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
Ce + est. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to be'.
